records.reason: Experiment 1 Task 1 directly retests the false-belief helping finding from Buttelmann et al. The results report that infants selected the toy's actual location as in the original; the General Discussion explicitly says this finding was replicated. The only supplied shipped original is Knudsen and Liszkowski (2011/2012), a different paper.
records.location: Experiment 1, Task 1 Results; General Discussion; References
records.omission_quote: Fifty-nine of the 94 participants (62.8%) first touched or opened the box containing the tiger; the remaining 35 first touched or opened the empty box E1 acted on. This distribution differed significantly from chance (z(93) = 2.37, P < 0.05). Thus, as in Buttelmann and colleagues’ original study (2009), 1.5-year-old infants were more likely to help not by opening the box the experimenter was pulling on, but by retrieving the toy the experimenter falsely believed to be in that box.
records.identity_quote: Buttelmann, D., Carpenter, M., & Tomasello, M. (2009). Eighteen-month-old infants show false belief understanding in an active helping paradigm.
